```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)

```

```{r}
df <- read_csv("datos_combinados.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cat("Filas originales:", nrow(df), " | Columnas:", ncol(df), "\n")
```
```{r}
upper_cols <- c("DEPREG","MUPREG","MESREG","AÑOREG","DIAOCU","MESOCU","AÑOOCU",
                "DEPOCU","MUPOCU","EDADHOM","EDADMUJ","PPERHOM","PPERMUJ",
                "NACHOM","NACMUJ","ESCHOM","ESCMUJ","CIUOHOM","CIUOMUJ")
lower_cols <- c("depreg","mupreg","mesreg","añoreg","diaocu","mesocu","añoocu",
                "depocu","mupocu","edadhom","edadmuj","grethom","gretmuj",
                "nachom","nacmuj","escohom","escomuj","ocupahom","ocupamuj")
 
for (i in seq_along(upper_cols)) {
  l <- lower_cols[i]; u <- upper_cols[i]
  df[[l]] <- ifelse(is.na(df[[l]]), df[[u]], df[[l]])
}
df <- df %>% select(all_of(c(lower_cols, "año del dato")))
cat("Despues de unificar:", nrow(df), "x", ncol(df), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Edades: 999 es codigo de "ignorado"; aplicamos rangos validos.
# Educacion: 9 es "ignorado". Como la variable respuesta se construye desde
# escohom/escomuj, mantener 9 introducira clasificaciones ficticias.
df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(edadhom < 100, edadmuj < 100,
         edadhom >= 18, edadmuj >= 14,
         escohom != 9, escomuj != 9)
cat("Despues de filtrado:", nrow(df_clean), "registros\n")
```

```{r Variables de respuesta}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(nivel_edu_pareja = case_when(
    escohom == escomuj ~ "Educacion_similar",
    escohom >  escomuj ~ "Esposo_mas_educado",
    escohom <  escomuj ~ "Esposa_mas_educada"
  ),
  nivel_edu_pareja = factor(nivel_edu_pareja))
 
cat("\nDistribucion de la variable respuesta:\n")
print(table(df_clean$nivel_edu_pareja))
cat("\nPorcentajes:\n")
print(round(prop.table(table(df_clean$nivel_edu_pareja)) * 100, 2))
```
```{r Ingenería de estadísticas}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(
    dif_edad     = edadhom - edadmuj,
    dif_edad_abs = abs(dif_edad),
    edad_prom    = (edadhom + edadmuj) / 2,
    esposo_mayor = as.integer(edadhom > edadmuj),
    edad_min     = pmin(edadhom, edadmuj),
    edad_max     = pmax(edadhom, edadmuj)
  )
```

```{r Seleccion de predictoras (sin data leakage)}
features_num <- c("edadhom","edadmuj","dif_edad","dif_edad_abs","edad_prom",
                  "esposo_mayor","edad_min","edad_max",
                  "mesreg","mesocu","diaocu","añoreg","añoocu","año del dato")
features_cat <- c("depreg","depocu","grethom","gretmuj",
                  "nachom","nacmuj","ocupahom","ocupamuj")
```

```{r Tratamiento de NAs y conversion a factor}
for (col in features_cat) {
  df_clean[[col]] <- as.character(df_clean[[col]])
  df_clean[[col]][is.na(df_clean[[col]])] <- "desconocido"
  df_clean[[col]] <- as.factor(df_clean[[col]])
}
for (col in features_num) {
  if (any(is.na(df_clean[[col]]))) {
    df_clean[[col]][is.na(df_clean[[col]])] <- median(df_clean[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}
 
# randomForest tiene un limite de 53 niveles por factor. Para variables con
# muchas categorias (ocupahom, mupocu, mupreg) agrupamos las menos frecuentes
# en "Otros". Nos quedamos con las top 50 mas frecuentes por variable.
collapse_levels <- function(x, top_n = 50) {
  freqs <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)
  keep  <- names(freqs)[seq_len(min(top_n, length(freqs)))]
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[!x %in% keep] <- "Otros"
  factor(x)
}
for (col in features_cat) {
  if (nlevels(df_clean[[col]]) > 50) {
    df_clean[[col]] <- collapse_levels(df_clean[[col]], top_n = 50)
  }
}
 
# Renombrar la columna con espacio porque randomForest no la acepta
df_clean <- df_clean %>% rename(ano_dato = `año del dato`,
                                anoreg   = `añoreg`,
                                anoocu   = `añoocu`)
features_num <- gsub("año del dato", "ano_dato", features_num)
features_num <- gsub("añoreg", "anoreg", features_num)
features_num <- gsub("añoocu", "anoocu", features_num)
 
predictoras <- c(features_num, features_cat)
cat("\nNumero de predictoras:", length(predictoras), "\n")
```

```{r Split train/test}
idx <- createDataPartition(df_clean$nivel_edu_pareja, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train <- df_clean[idx, ]
test  <- df_clean[-idx, ]
cat("Train:", nrow(train), " | Test:", nrow(test), "\n")
 
```
```{r Balseline}
clase_mayoritaria <- names(sort(table(train$nivel_edu_pareja), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
acc_baseline <- mean(test$nivel_edu_pareja == clase_mayoritaria)
cat(sprintf("\nBaseline (predecir siempre '%s'): %.4f\n",
            clase_mayoritaria, acc_baseline))
 
```
```{r Random Forest con class weights balanceados}
# classwt compensa el desbalance: a la clase mayoritaria se le da menor peso.
freqs <- table(train$nivel_edu_pareja)
classwt <- as.numeric(1 / freqs)
classwt <- classwt / sum(classwt)
names(classwt) <- names(freqs)
 
formula_rf <- as.formula(paste("nivel_edu_pareja ~",
                               paste(predictoras, collapse = " + ")))
 
cat("\nEntrenando Random Forest...\n")
rf_modelo <- randomForest(
  formula_rf,
  data       = train,
  ntree      = 300,
  mtry       = floor(sqrt(length(predictoras))),  # ~5
  nodesize   = 5,
  classwt    = classwt,
  importance = TRUE
)
print(rf_modelo)
```

```{r  Evaluacion en test}
pred_test  <- predict(rf_modelo, newdata = test)
pred_train <- predict(rf_modelo, newdata = train)
acc_train  <- mean(pred_train == train$nivel_edu_pareja)
acc_test   <- mean(pred_test  == test$nivel_edu_pareja)
 
cat(sprintf("\nAccuracy train: %.4f\n", acc_train))
cat(sprintf("Accuracy test:  %.4f\n", acc_test))
 
cm <- confusionMatrix(pred_test, test$nivel_edu_pareja)
cat("\n=== Matriz de confusion (test) ===\n")
print(cm$table)
cat("\n=== Metricas por clase ===\n")
print(round(cm$byClass[, c("Precision","Recall","F1")], 4))
```
```{r Validacion cruzada 5-fold}

cat("\nCross-validation 5-fold...\n")
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5,
                     classProbs = FALSE, savePredictions = "final")
cv_rf <- train(
  formula_rf,
  data      = df_clean,
  method    = "rf",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid  = data.frame(mtry = floor(sqrt(length(predictoras)))),
  ntree     = 200   # algo menor para acelerar el CV
)
cat(sprintf("CV accuracy: %.4f +/- %.4f\n",
            cv_rf$results$Accuracy, cv_rf$results$AccuracySD))
```

```{r Importancia de variables }
imp_df <- data.frame(
  feature    = rownames(importance(rf_modelo)),
  importance = importance(rf_modelo)[, "MeanDecreaseGini"]
) %>% arrange(desc(importance))
cat("\n=== Top 12 variables mas importantes ===\n")
print(head(imp_df, 12))
```


```{r Graficos con ggplot2 }
# Matriz de confusion
cm_df <- as.data.frame(cm$table)
colnames(cm_df) <- c("Predicho", "Real", "Frecuencia")
g_cm <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicho, y = Real, fill = Frecuencia)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Frecuencia), size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2E75B6") +
  labs(title = "Matriz de confusion - Random Forest",
       x = "Predicho", y = "Real") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
print(g_cm)
 
# Feature importance (top 15)
top_imp <- head(imp_df, 15)

g_imp <- ggplot(top_imp, aes(x = reorder(feature, importance), 
                              y = importance, 
                              fill = importance)) +  
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", importance)),  
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +           
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Top 15 variables mas importantes - Random Forest",
       x = NULL, y = "Importancia (Mean Decrease Gini)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")                      
print(g_imp)


#  Comparacion baseline vs modelo
comp_df <- data.frame(
  Modelo   = factor(c("Baseline\n(clase mayoritaria)",
                      "Random Forest\n(test)",
                      "Random Forest\n(CV 5-fold)"),
                    levels = c("Baseline\n(clase mayoritaria)",
                               "Random Forest\n(test)",
                               "Random Forest\n(CV 5-fold)")),
  Accuracy = c(acc_baseline, acc_test, cv_rf$results$Accuracy),
  err      = c(0, 0, cv_rf$results$AccuracySD)
)
g_comp <- ggplot(comp_df, aes(x = Modelo, y = Accuracy, fill = Modelo)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Accuracy - err, ymax = Accuracy + err),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", Accuracy)),
            vjust = -0.8, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#cccccc", "#2E86AB", "#A23B72")) +
  labs(title = "Comparacion: baseline vs Random Forest",
       y = "Accuracy", x = NULL) +
  ylim(0, 0.75) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
print(g_comp)
```

```{r inciso 4}
# 1. Definir el control de entrenamiento (Validación Cruzada 5-fold)
ctrl_tune <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)

# 2. Crear la rejilla de parámetros (Grid Search)

grid_rf <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2, 5, 10, 15, 20))

cat("\nEntrenando multiples modelos Random Forest para encontrar el mejor ajuste...\n")

# 3. Entrenar los modelos

rf_tuneado <- train(
  formula_rf,
  data      = train, 
  method    = "rf",
  trControl = ctrl_tune,
  tuneGrid  = grid_rf,
  ntree     = 200 
)

# 4. Mostrar los resultados de los 5 modelos
cat("\n=== Resultados de la Búsqueda del Mejor Modelo ===\n")
print(rf_tuneado)

# 5. Gráfica para justificar la elección (Complejidad vs Accuracy)
ggplot(rf_tuneado) + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  labs(title = "Rendimiento del Modelo según el parámetro 'mtry'",
       x = "Cantidad de variables aleatorias por división (mtry)",
       y = "Accuracy (Precisión en Validación Cruzada)")

# 6. Extraer el mejor modelo final
modelo_final <- rf_tuneado$finalModel
cat("\nEl mejor parámetro encontrado fue mtry =", rf_tuneado$bestTune$mtry, "\n")
```
